QUOTE: "Traversal (`chain_trace`) drops them. The flat list keeps them, because filtering would remove 21.3% of this repo's edges and 79.8% of a real C++ target."
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says the flat list keeps fuzzy edges while traversal drops them, but it gives a different reason (filtering would remove too many edges). It never says that a walk expands each hop, so a single fuzzy edge multiplies into a wrong subtree.
